column3: Not many of you should become teachers, my brothers and sisters, knowing that we will receive a greater judgment.
For we all stumble in many ways. If anyone does not stumble in word, this one is a mature person, able also to bridle the whole body.
Now if we put bits into horses’ mouths so that they obey us, we also guide their whole body.
Look also at ships: though so large and driven by strong winds, they are guided by a very small rudder wherever the impulse of the one steering wishes.
So also the tongue is a small member and boasts great things. Look how small a fire sets ablaze how great a forest.
And the tongue is a fire, the world of unrighteousness. The tongue is set among our members, staining the whole body, setting on fire the course of life, and itself set on fire by Gehenna.
For every kind of beast and bird, reptile and sea creature, is tamed and has been tamed by humankind,
but no human being is able to tame the tongue. It is a restless evil, full of deadly poison.
With it we bless the Lord and Father, and with it we curse people who have been made according to the likeness of God.
From the same mouth come blessing and cursing. My brothers and sisters, these things ought not to be so.
Does a spring pour out from the same opening both sweet and bitter water?
Can a fig tree, my brothers and sisters, produce olives, or a grapevine figs? Neither can salt water produce fresh.
Who is wise and understanding among you? Let that person show from good conduct their works in the gentleness of wisdom.
But if you have bitter jealousy and selfish ambition in your heart, do not boast and lie against the truth.
This is not the wisdom coming down from above, but earthly, natural, demonic.
For where jealousy and selfish ambition are, there is disorder and every worthless practice.
But the wisdom from above is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, open to reason, full of mercy and good fruits, impartial, sincere.
And a fruit of righteousness is sown in peace by those who make peace.
